problem: I'm building an alumni mentorship network in Jac. Mentor relationships are typed edges carrying the year each mentorship started. Create several mentorships between alumni, then write a finder walker that traverses only Mentor edges and filters on the start year so it can list everyone mentored since a given year.

I'm encoding a family tree in Jac with ParentOf edges pointing from parents to children. Starting from someone in the middle generation, write a genealogy walker that visits that person's parents by walking incoming edges, then lists everyone directly linked in either direction, and stops once done.

I'm building a package-routing prototype in Jac. Hubs are nodes (one flagged as the depot) and Route edges carry transit hours plus a frozen-cargo policy. Dispatch runs take the destination and whether cargo is frozen as spawn parameters; frozen shipments may only ride frozen-safe routes, the router stops as soon as it delivers or hits a dead end, and the depot prints each run's outcome from the returned reports.

Help me encode a CS curriculum in Jac: prerequisite edges form a chain built in one chained statement, and a lab course is co-requisite with its lecture via a bidirectional edge. A degree planner walker should skip courses the student already completed, note any co-requisite partners it meets along the way, and finish as soon as the senior capstone gets scheduled, reporting the planned credit total.

Simulate a cave expedition through three chained chambers (Mouth, Tunnel, Crystal Cavern). Print ENTER as the explorer reaches each chamber and EXIT when they leave it, so the transcript shows departures unwinding in reverse order of arrival.

Roll up budgets across our org chart (HQ containing Engineering with Backend and Frontend, plus Sales): each unit's subtotal is its own budget plus all its sub-units' finalized subtotals, computed bottom-up as the auditor backs out of each unit. Print each unit's subtotal as it completes and the company total.

Crawl a small social graph: for each profile list who they timed-follow and what they posted, stamping how long each timed follow has been active during edge traversal itself, and never crawl the same profile twice even though some profiles are reachable by several paths.

Read a chat channel's reactions: show which account reacted to each message via reaction edges, covering moderator pins (only moderators can create them), echoes, and plain reactions from regular users.

Compare a standard courier and an express courier over the same depot chain (HUB, MID, AIR). The express courier overrides depot handling to expedite double the parcels. Print pickup lines for both and their totals.

Simulate a day at the midway: riders too short for the Viper coaster are turned away for the rest of their outing, rides award fun points, and food stalls and gift shops ring up purchases with receipts. Summarize fun points and spending for one tall and one short guest.

Build a dungeon crawler: heroes loot treasure rooms, take damage from traps (collapsing ends the run), retreat from bosses that are too strong, and as they back out each chamber reports its complete subtree gold bottom-up. A rogue subclass sneaks the same dungeon for double loot without fighting.

Our power-grid model stores transmission lines between substations, each carrying its capacity in megawatts. Walk the grid from every substation and list only the neighbours reachable over lines rated above 400 MW -- weaker lines can't carry the scheduled transfer.

Our knowledge wiki has articles citing other articles, and articles written by authors. Starting from one article, follow its citations onward to discover the authors behind the cited work, mixing both relationship kinds in a single walk.

Store a family tree as parent-to-child links. For every person, work out their siblings by going up to their shared parents and back down to the other children, and report each person's full sibling list.

Print a fare board for our flight network. The flights themselves carry the data -- flight number and ticket price -- so read the connections themselves rather than just the destination airports, and list every departure from each airport with its fare.

Send a delivery van from our depot across town to Seaside. Every road charges a toll collected as the van crosses it, and the van should keep a running total of tolls paid, printing the bill at each town it arrives in and the grand total at the end.

Our power grid's lines meter current as inspectors cross them. Audit the grid twice: once walking substation to substation normally, and once in a mode where the inspector steps onto each line itself. Show that meters only record in the second mode.

A courier serves districts either by highway or by ferry depending on the dispatch mode chosen at run time. Run two deliveries with different modes and let the courier pick which kind of connection to follow while it walks, reporting where each run can and cannot go.

I'm building a small social app and want a 'people you may know' feature. Given one member, I need to look at their friends' friends, skip anyone they are already connected to, and rank the rest by how many mutual connections they share. Can you show me a complete program that does this on a sample network?

I need a scheduler for our CI pipeline. Tasks have durations, some cannot start until others finish, and I want a valid execution order that respects all prerequisites plus the total time if tasks run one after another. If there is a cycle among the remaining tasks it should say so instead of getting stuck silently.

I'm playing with a knowledge graph of people, companies and cities connected by relations like works-at, lives-in and headquartered-in. From one person I want to answer questions like where their coworkers live, which companies are based in their own city, and which colleagues joined recently. A runnable demo answering several such multi-hop questions from a sample graph would help a lot.

For my supply chain dashboard I want to simulate weekend orders flowing upstream. Stores place demand, depots pass received demand further up, and when a facility has multiple suppliers the demand should split proportionally to each lane's capacity. At the end I need the accumulated backlog per facility printed out.

I'm designing access control for a document system. Roles grant specific permissions directly and also inherit everything from parent roles, sometimes through more than one path. For any starting role I need the deduplicated set of effective permissions, sorted, computed over a sample hierarchy that includes a diamond-shaped inheritance case.

I dispatch delivery drivers between cities connected by toll roads. As a quick heuristic, the driver should just take the cheapest road out of their current city, never revisit a city, and keep going until reaching the destination or hitting a dead end. I want the route and total cost printed even if the greedy choice is not globally optimal - that is part of the point.

I'm building search over a library catalog. Each book has a title, author, year and tags, and given a query I want each book scored on where the query matches (title beats author beats tags) with a small bonus for newer books, then the top few matches shown ranked. Please include a mixed catalog so the ranking is actually visible.

Commuters keep asking our trip planner how many times they will have to change lines. My metro map is stations joined by track segments that belong to named lines; staying on one line is free, switching lines at a station costs one change. From an origin station I want the minimum number of changes to reach a destination, and a clear message when a station is not connected to the network at all.

I'm prototyping a disease model on a contact network. People have contact strengths with each other, infection spreads along contacts probabilistically each day, and I want to run a week-long simulation printing daily case counts. It must produce identical numbers on every run so I can compare interventions fairly.

I want to rank accounts in a follow graph by influence: every account starts with a base score and repeatedly shares its score evenly across the accounts it follows while collecting scores from its followers. Repeat the refinement passes until things settle, then print the leaderboard ordered by final score.

My forum shows engagement per discussion thread, but replies nest arbitrarily deep and every post's count should include all its descendants' likes, not just its own. Compute these rolled-up totals bottom-up for a couple of nested comment threads, then rank the top-level posts by total engagement.

My task app needs an edit endpoint. Clients only keep the id that creation reported back, so write a private walker that takes a jid string plus new title and done values, walks the caller's root until the jid matches, mutates the node in place, and stops early. A bogus id should simply produce no report.

My micro-blog needs a public feed: whoever calls publish, authenticated or not, hangs their post on the shared public graph and opens that single post to readers while ownership stays theirs. Use the shared root reachable from any request context and arm a read-level grant on each fresh post. Have the program print both the shared root's id and the current root's id so I can see they match on a plain CLI run.

My app keeps a docs cache that anyone may rebuild; openness here is an invariant of the type rather than a per-instance choice. Encode that once on the archetype with an access hook so every instance is open at WRITE level to every user, subtypes included. Pair it with an open edge type too, since edges are checked separately.

My recipe box needs search that feels ranked, not just filtered. Score each substring match by where the query appears -- recipe name beats cuisine beats ingredient, plus a small bonus for shorter names -- then sort best-first before reporting. Show the sorted hits for a query like 'curry'.

While debugging my app's graph I kept wanting a quick look at what's actually stored. Build a small IOU ledger, print each node's unique id, explicitly persist the nodes, flush pending changes, and dump the structure from the root. Keep it small enough that the dump is readable.
